title: On‑Prem Optimization Orchestrator: Offline Advisor + Policy Enforcement + Safe Defaults
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an orchestrator service that enables cost-optimization recommendations (batching/caching/quantization hints) for Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments while enforcing safe defaults, running in an offline/dry‑run sandbox, and applying changes only when policies and approvals pass. This ticket implements the advisor + policy layer and the safe‑apply/rollback protocol for on‑prem installs.
background: We already have hosted autotune advisors and several VPC-safe simulators in prod. On‑prem customers have stricter constraints: no external telemetry, delayed maintenance windows, and RBAC/Governance requirements. Past attempts to auto-apply tuner recommendations in private installs were blocked by security reviews or caused config drift during upgrades. We need an orchestrator that respects air‑gapped environments, runs offline simulations against local telemetry, enforces org policies, and supports safe staged applies with fast rollback.
objectives: 1) Produce deterministic batching/caching recommendations using local logs and a lightweight simulator. 2) Validate each recommendation against a policy matrix (latency SLO, memory cap, security safe list). 3) Provide a dry‑run offline mode that produces a signed apply plan and an observable rollback strategy. 4) Integrate with on‑prem RBAC and audit logs for approvals. 5) Ensure automated rollback succeeds within 5 minutes of a failed canary.
proposed_solution: Introduce a standalone binary 'onprem-optimizer-orchestrator' that runs inside the customer's VPC. The orchestrator ingests local request histograms and KV cache stats, runs a deterministic simulator to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs, emits a recommendations artifact (signed JSON), then evaluates recommendations against a configurable policy bundle. If recommendations pass policy and are marked for auto‑apply by the org, orchestrator executes a staged apply using a sandboxed control-plane connector and watches health checks; otherwise it surfaces the artifact for manual review. All actions append to local audit logs and produce compact metrics that can be exported to the customer's monitoring stack.
config_defaults: The orchestrator will ship with a hardened default profile: batching: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_batch_size=8, batching_window_ms=12; caching: prefix_cache_enabled=true, kv_cache_max_entries=10000 with eviction=LRU; quantization_hint=dynamic-8bit; apply_mode=manual-by-default; dry_run_enabled=true; auto_rollback=true. Defaults are conservative to avoid memory blowouts on small GPU hosts.
offline_mode_behaviour: Offline/dry-run mode performs a deterministic simulation using local traces and a fixed random seed. It writes an apply-plan artifact which includes resource delta estimates, required steps, and a 'rollback recipe' (sequence of reverse steps). Dry-run must not change runtime config. Operators can run the apply-plan through a verifier that will re-simulate and produce a verification token (signed).
policy_enforcement_matrix: latency_slo: ensure p95 change <= +10% for critical routes
memory_budget: no recommendation can increase peak GPU memory usage beyond 90% of configured host_limit
security_allowlist: disallow any kernel-level or syscall changes without security-approval
approval_flow: auto-apply only if org_policy.auto_apply=true and approvals >= 1 from ops team
rollback_guarantee: apply must be reversible within 5 minutes using stored checkpoints
acceptance_criteria: Local simulator produces stable cost and latency deltas for five representative traces with variance < 3% between runs
Policy engine blocks any recommendation that would breach memory_budget or latency_slo in unit tests
Dry-run create + verify flow outputs a signed apply-plan artifact and a matching rollback recipe
Staged apply completes canary rollout to 10% of hosts and health-check watchdog initiates rollback on injected failure within 60s
All orchestrator actions are logged to local audit file and produce an entry in the customer's SIEM-compatible format
rollout_plan: 1) Merge orchestrator binary behind feature flag. 2) Install to an internal staging on‑prem cluster and run 3 synthetic workloads. 3) Run partner pilot with two existing on‑prem customers (opt-in). 4) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry and signed approvals, enable auto-apply for non-production namespaces. 5) Gradually raise canary percentage to 100% with nightly windows. Document runbooks.
rollback_plan: Every apply creates a rollback artifact that contains: previous runtime snapshot, kernel config pointers, and a script to revert changes. The orchestrator will keep a rolling 7-day snapshot store (config space only) and will attempt automated rollback on failing health checks. If automated rollback fails, a high-severity incident is triggered and runbook instructs on preservation of snapshot and contacting oncall security and infra.
test_plan: Unit tests for simulator determinism; policy engine fuzz tests; e2e in isolated on‑prem staging with injected latency and memory failures; chaos test that simulates partial failures of 3 hosts during canary; verification harness to confirm rollback recipe reverts state consistently in <5m. Create synthetic traces (chat bursts, long token sequences) to validate batching/caching behavior.
notes: Key trade-offs: conservative defaults reduce immediate cost wins but materially lower blast radius. We opted for signed artifacts and local audit-only writes to respect air-gapped customers. Long-term roadmap includes a lightweight differential snapshot proto to reduce rollback size. Need follow-up to integrate with KMS/HSM for artifact signing in regulated customers.
blockers: Final sign-off from security (KMS integration) and Legal for automated rollback in certain regulated customers. Also need perf kernel profiles for on‑prem GPU variants (Ampere v.s. older T4s).
